results.name: Parcel_Lines
results.title: Parcel Boundary Lines
results.description:
Data is maintained by the Lee County Property Appraiser and is synchronized weekly

Overview

This feature service provides detailed parcel boundary line data for Lee County, Florida, maintained by the Lee County Property Appraiser. It supports land records management, cadastral mapping, and various property-related analyses in the county.

Feature Layer

  • Parcel Lines: This layer represents the boundary lines of land parcels within Lee County. It includes precise geometric details such as bearings, distances, radii, arc lengths, and angles that define individual parcel boundaries. Various types of parcels are captured, including traditional PLSS townships, sections, special surveys, ownership boundaries, and encumbrances. The lines are categorized by their function, such as boundary lines, connection lines, radial (system-generated) lines, and road frontages. Attributes also track the legal status and historical information of each parcel boundary line, allowing for temporal analyses and legal reference. This layer is essential for cadastral surveys, property ownership verification, and land use planning.

Geographic Coverage

The service covers all parcels within Lee County, Florida, providing comprehensive spatial data critical for county-level property appraisal, land management, and government planning efforts.

Use Cases

  • Support for property appraisal and taxation through accurate parcel boundary delineation.
  • Assistance in land ownership and legal boundary dispute resolution by providing detailed legal boundary data.
  • Facilitation of urban planning, zoning, and development permit processes by local government agencies.
  • Provision of precise parcel fabric data to surveying professionals and GIS analysts for mapping and land use studies.

Data Maintenance and Licensing

The data is regularly updated by the Lee County Property Appraiser to ensure accuracy and currency. Users should note the licensing terms, which disclaim warranties and limit liability, emphasizing that the data is a public resource provided "as is" without guarantees on accuracy or fitness for a particular purpose.

results.name: Subdivisions_and_Condominiums
results.title: Subdivisions and Condominiums
results.description:
Data maintained by the Lee County Property Appraiser. Updates to this layer are synchronized weekly.

Overview

This feature service provides detailed geographic and attribute data concerning subdivisions and condominiums within Lee County, Florida. It serves as a critical resource for property appraisal, land use planning, and legal documentation.

Feature Layer Details

  • FabricSubdivisions: This layer represents the boundaries and details of subdivisions and condominiums. It includes legal descriptions, conveyance types (such as Subdivision, Condominium, Assessor Plat, and various land grant types), and associated metadata such as recording document links, municipality jurisdiction codes, and official stated areas with units. The layer captures both spatial (polygon geometries with area and perimeter measurements) and attribute information, facilitating comprehensive land parcel representation.

Geographic Coverage

The data specifically covers subdivisions and condominiums within Lee County, Florida, providing localized details to support county-specific property management and planning needs.

Use Cases

  • Property appraisal and taxation by county authorities.
  • Land use planning and zoning analysis.
  • Legal reference for land conveyance and subdivisions.
  • Supporting public access to authoritative property subdivision data.

results.name: TDR_Sending_Parcels
results.title: Collier County Transfer of Development Rights Sending Parcels
results.description:
Overview

This feature service provides spatial data related to Transfer of Development Rights (TDR) within a defined region of Lee County, Florida. The service supports land use planning efforts by detailing parcels designated as sending areas and assessing their potential for development rights transfer.

Feature Layers
  • TDR Sending Area: This layer represents parcels identified as sending areas in the TDR program. It includes polygon geometries delineating parcel boundaries with area and perimeter measurements. These sending areas contribute development rights for transfer and are essential for managing land conservation and controlling growth.
  • TDR Potential: This layer evaluates the potential of parcels to send development rights, including classifications that indicate suitability for participation in TDR programs. It features polygon data measuring parcel area and length, aiding the analysis of which parcels can effectively contribute to the transfer of development rights.
Geographic Coverage

The service covers portions of Lee County in southwestern Florida, focusing on parcels relevant to regional planning for sustainable growth and development rights management.

Use Cases
  • Urban and regional planners can identify and assess parcels eligible to send development rights, facilitating better land use decisions.
  • Policy makers and land managers may use this data to support strategies that balance development and conservation.
  • GIS professionals can integrate these layers into broader environmental and planning analyses to inform community growth and land preservation efforts.
results.snippet: Spatial data delineating Transfer of Development Rights sending parcels and their development potential supporting land use planning in Lee County Florida.

results.name: Parcel_Lots
results.title: Parcel Lot Boundaries
results.description:
Data maintained by the Lee County Property Appraiser. Updates to this layer are synchronized weekly.

Overview

This Feature Service provides detailed geographic data on parcel lots located in Lee County, Florida. It captures essential spatial and descriptive information about individual land parcels, facilitating land management and planning activities.

Feature Layers

  • Lots: This layer represents the boundaries and attributes of parcel lots in the region. Each parcel includes a unique identifier and descriptive information such as lot number, name, and stated area, typically measured in acres. The layer also maintains data on the geometric properties of each lot, including area and perimeter length, along with metadata documenting the creation and modification history of the parcel records.

Geographic Coverage

The data covers a geographic extent in Lee County, Florida, allowing local governments, planners, surveyors, and GIS professionals to analyze land parcels within this specific area.

Use Cases

  • Land use planning and zoning enforcement
  • Property management and cadastral mapping
  • Infrastructure development and environmental assessment

results.name: Florida_Statewide_Cadastral
results.title: Florida Statewide Parcels
results.description:
The Florida Department of Revenue’s Property Tax Oversight(PTO) program collects parcel level Geographic Information System (GIS) data files every April from all of Florida’s 67 county property appraisers’ offices. This GIS data was exported from these file submissions in August 2026. The GIS parcel polygon features have been joined with thereal property roll (Name – Address – Legal, or NAL)file. No line work was adjusted between county boundaries.The polygon data set represents the information property appraisers gathered from the legal description on deeds, lot layout of recorded plats, declaration of condominium documents, recorded and unrecorded surveys.

Individual parcel data is updated continually by each county property appraiser as needed. The GIS linework and related attributions for the statewide parcel map are updated annually by the Department every August.  Minor data maintenance is also completed every May and November. The dataset extends countywide and is attribute by Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) code.

DOR reference with FIPS county codes and attribution definitions - https://fgio.maps.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=55e830fd6c8948baae1601fbfc33a3b2

If you discover the inadvertent release of a confidential record exempt from disclosure pursuant to Chapter 119, Florida Statutes, public records laws, immediately notify the Department of Revenue at 850-717-6570 and your local Florida Property Appraisers’ Office.
